long_biography.plain_text:
Brewing standards became an executive discipline for August Busch III. Trained at Chicago’s Siebel Institute, he personally led twice-weekly beer tastings and toured company facilities, treating product consistency and operational detail as responsibilities of the top office. That intensity shaped Anheuser-Busch’s response when Miller challenged its market position.

Busch took control after persuading directors to replace his father as chief executive in 1975. He then oversaw new breweries, product launches and international expansion as the company’s domestic beer share more than doubled. Patrick Stokes succeeded him in 2002, becoming the first executive outside the Busch family to run Anheuser-Busch’s day-to-day operations. Busch later retired from executive duties.
